title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
text: geom_latex() works like geom_text() interprets label aesthetic LaTeX math string.
code: df <- data.frame(   x = 1:3,   y = 1:3,   eq = c("x^2", "\\frac{a}{b}", "\\sum_{i=1}^n x_i") )  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, label = eq)) +   geom_latex() +   theme_minimal()

title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
text: Map size (font size points) colour aesthetics usual:
code: df$col <- c("red", "blue", "darkgreen")  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, label = eq, colour = col, size = c(14, 18, 14))) +   geom_latex() +   scale_colour_identity() +   scale_size_identity() +   theme_minimal()

what: Adding equation annotations to a scatter plot
title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
text: common use case annotating regression fit model equation. Use annotate("latex", ...) single annotations — delegates GeomLatex internally avoids creating data frame automatically hides legend.
code: fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars) b0 <- round(coef(fit)[1], 1) b1 <- round(coef(fit)[2], 1) r2 <- round(summary(fit)$r.squared, 3)  eq_label <- sprintf("\\hat{y} = %s %s x, \\quad R^2 = %s",                      b0, b1, r2)  ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +   annotate("latex", x = 4, y = 30, label = eq_label, size = 12) +   theme_minimal() #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
text: element_latex() replaces text theme element label rendered LaTeX math.  Dollar-sign delimiters ($...$) stripped automatically, "\\frac{}{b}" "$\\frac{}{b}$" produce output.
code: ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   labs(     x = "$\\beta_1 \\cdot x + \\beta_0$",     y = "$\\mathrm{mpg}$"   ) +   theme(     axis.title.x = element_latex(fontsize = 14),     axis.title.y = element_latex(fontsize = 14)   )

title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
text: can use geom_latex() element_latex() together:
code: df <- data.frame(   x = c(1, 2, 3),   y = c(1, 4, 9),   eq = c("1^2", "2^2", "3^2") )  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, label = eq)) +   geom_point(size = 3) +   geom_latex(vjust = -1, fontsize = 14) +   labs(     x = "$n$",     y = "$n^2$",     title = "Perfect squares"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     axis.title.x = element_latex(fontsize = 14),     axis.title.y = element_latex(fontsize = 14)   )

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: gridmicrotex renders LaTeX math equations native R grid graphics objects (grobs). uses MicroTeX C++ library layout engine — MicroTeX parses LaTeX, builds TeX box model, computes exact glyph coordinates. package intercepts layout data maps native grid primitives (pathGrob, segmentsGrob, rectGrob, textGrob), producing gTree works R graphics device resolution. Key features: external LaTeX installation required — MicroTeX fully embedded Resolution-independent vector output R devices (PNG, PDF, SVG, …) Full math support: fractions, roots, integrals, matrices, Greek letters, accents, delimiters, Multiple math fonts (Latin Modern Math, XITS Math, Garamond Math, TeX Gyre DejaVu Math) Color support via \textcolor{} ggplot2 integration geom_latex() element_latex() CJK multilingual text \text{} blocks

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: core function latex_grob(), returns grid grob:  quick rendering, use grid.latex():
code: g <- latex_grob("\\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}", fontsize = 24) grid::grid.newpage() grid::grid.draw(g) grid::grid.newpage() grid.latex("\\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^2", fontsize = 28)

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: Control placement x, y, hjust, vjust:
code: grid::grid.newpage() grid.latex("E = mc^2", x = 0.2, y = 0.7, hjust = 0, fontsize = 24) grid.latex("F = ma", x = 0.2, y = 0.3, hjust = 0, fontsize = 24)

text: Set formula color via gp, use \textcolor{} within LaTeX:
code: grid::grid.newpage() grid.latex(   "\\textcolor{red}{\\alpha} + \\textcolor{blue}{\\beta} = \\gamma",   fontsize = 28 )

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: package bundles Latin Modern Math (default), XITS Math, TeX Gyre DejaVu Math. users, easiest workflow : List available math fonts available_math_fonts() Select one set_math_font() Render formulas normally (OTF/CLM paths needed)  can still override font per call via math_font:  Use available_math_fonts() list loaded fonts check_fonts() diagnostic report.
code: available_math_fonts() #> [1] "Garamond-Math"             "LatinModernMath-Regular"   #> [3] "TeXGyreDejaVuMath-Regular" "XITS Math" set_math_font("xits") grid::grid.newpage() grid.latex("\\int_0^1 f(x)\\,dx", fontsize = 24) # Switch back to Latin Modern Math set_math_font("lm") grid::grid.newpage() grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(2, 1))) grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1)) grid.latex("\\int_0^1 f(x)\\,dx", fontsize = 24) grid::upViewport() grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 2)) grid.latex("\\int_0^1 f(x)\\,dx", fontsize = 24, math_font = "xits") grid::upViewport(2)

code: load_font("path/to/MyFont.otf")

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: gridmicrotex supports two rendering modes math glyphs: "typeface" (default): Renders glyphs native text using math font’s typeface. produces selectable, searchable, accessible text PDF SVG output. Requires math font (e.g., Latin Modern Math) installed system, device supports font embedding (e.g., ragg::agg_png(), svglite::svglite(), grDevices::cairo_pdf()). devices support typeface rendering (e.g., base pdf() device), package automatically falls back path mode warning. "path": Renders glyph filled vector path. works R graphics devices produces pixel-perfect output. However, text PDF/SVG output selectable searchable. Important: use showtext::showtext_auto() typeface mode. showtext package globally intercepts text rendering converts vector paths. silently defeats typeface mode, causing math glyphs appear paths instead native text — even devices like svglite ragg fully support font embedding. need showtext parts plot, disable drawing LaTeX formulas:
code: # Default typeface mode (selectable text in PDF/SVG) grid.latex("E = mc^2", fontsize = 24)  # Explicit path mode (works everywhere, but text is not selectable) grid.latex("E = mc^2", fontsize = 24, render_mode = "path") showtext::showtext_auto(FALSE) grid.latex("E = mc^2", fontsize = 24)  # typeface mode works correctly

code: grid::grid.newpage() grid.latex("x^2 + \\text{你好}", fontsize = 24, gp = grid::gpar(fontfamily = "sans"))
